findings.reason: as written the node's gate either still fails at head for a correct fix or passes at base, and only a fixture carrying the same-state re-announcement row both reproduces the incident and is falsified by the declared control.
findings.text: the done-when drives only working→blocked, blocked→working, working→completed_unpromoted, "with the rows more than the settle window apart"; with no same-state row between the stop and the resume, the run's remembered word is still `working` when the resume arrives (the stop is held as a noise opener — ticker.py:994,1664 — and released late at ticker.py:1614 without `_note_printed`), so the resume is withheld by the same-word gate at ticker.py:1633 before the start check at ticker.py:1642 is reached. Measured by driving RowPolicy with the three rows: at a 30 s and a 158 s stop→resume gap both base and the patched start set leave the row unprinted (the stated "working row" never appears at head), and at 340 s+ the row prints at base too, so the gate cannot fail there; adding the stream's own `blocked → blocked` row gives base=withheld, patched=printed at every gap.

findings.reason: a start pair keyed on the literal `exited_unfinished` would match no producer row, leaving a resume out of an exit still drawn halted; the fix is one word.
findings.text: the deliverable lists `exited_unfinished` among the stop states, but no surface emits that string: `exited_unfinished` is only a local boolean in the classifier (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:541) whereas the emitted classification and the PANE_STATES halted key are both `exited-unfinished` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:300, reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py:38), and the plan's own §5 vocabulary uses the hyphen form.
